name: Universal Health Services
description: Universal Health Services runs hospitals: 29 acute care hospitals in the US (plus 35 free-standing emergency departments and outpatient centers) and 346 inpatient behavioral health facilities in the US, UK (Cygnet) and Puerto Rico. Patients and their insurers, Medicare and Medicaid pay it for each admission or day of care. The behavioral health business is the profit engine: 43 percent of revenue but about 58 percent of segment pre-tax profit, at a 19.7 percent pre-tax margin versus 10.5 percent for acute care. Net revenues were $17.36 billion in 2025, up 9.7 percent.

gics.note: Conventional filing: Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (read 2026-09-30) gives sector Health Care and sub-industry Health Care Facilities; industry group and industry not listed there, left null. SEC SIC 8062.

hq.note: Per Wikipedia List of S&P 500 companies

employees.note: Approximately 101,500 total employees, about 88,100 located in the US (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Acute Care Hospital Services
businessLines.how: Charges per admission, per patient day or per procedure, paid by commercial insurers at negotiated rates and by Medicare and Medicaid at government rates; volume (admissions) and revenue per adjusted admission (up 5.4% in 2025 on a same-facility basis) drive revenue.
businessLines.description: 29 inpatient acute care hospitals, 35 free-standing emergency departments, 13 outpatient centers and 1 surgical hospital in the US (including Cedar Hill Regional Medical Center, opened Q2 2025, and George Washington University Hospital in Washington, D.C.), and a commercial health insurer.

revenue.note: Net revenue from reportable segments; +$982M or +11.0% vs 2024 (about 8.9B), same-facility +8.5%. Texas, Nevada and California are the largest states by facility revenue.

businessLines.revenueNote: Net revenue from reportable segments; +$982M or +11.0% vs 2024 (about 8.9B), same-facility +8.5%. Texas, Nevada and California are the largest states by facility revenue.

operatingProfit.note: Segment income before income taxes about $1.05B (10.5% of net revenues) vs $840M (9.4%); includes a $49M pre-tax loss at the newly opened Cedar Hill hospital. Share computed over the sum of the two segments' pre-tax income (about $2.51B), which is higher than consolidated pre-tax income of $1.97B because of non-segment expenses.

businessLines.name: Behavioral Health Care Services
businessLines.how: Per-patient-day charges for inpatient psychiatric and substance-abuse stays, paid by commercial insurers, state Medicaid programs, Medicare and, in the UK, the NHS and local authorities; occupancy and length of stay drive revenue.
businessLines.description: 346 inpatient behavioral health facilities and 119 outpatient facilities: 182 inpatient and 110 outpatient in the US, 161 inpatient and 2 outpatient in the UK (Cygnet Health Care), and 3 inpatient and 7 outpatient in Puerto Rico (as listed in the FY2025 10-K).

revenue.note: Net revenue from reportable segments; same-facility +7.7% on a same-facility basis (+$516M)

businessLines.revenueNote: Net revenue from reportable segments; same-facility +7.7% on a same-facility basis (+$516M)

operatingProfit.note: Segment income before income taxes about $1.46B (19.7% of net revenues) vs $1.36B (19.7%), +7.7%. Share computed over the sum of both segments' pre-tax income.

brands.name: Cygnet Health Care (UK behavioral)
brands.share: 161 inpatient behavioral facilities in the UK of 346 total inpatient behavioral facilities (47%); UK revenue not extracted

brands.name: George Washington University Hospital
brands.share: Acute care hospital in Washington, D.C.; revenue not separately reported

brands.name: Cedar Hill Regional Medical Center
brands.share: New acute care hospital in Washington, D.C. opened Q2 2025; $49M pre-tax loss in 2025

brands.name: Texas operations
brands.share: 7 acute hospitals, 16 free-standing emergency departments, 20 inpatient and 14 outpatient behavioral facilities; combined 16% of consolidated net revenues
